passages.text: Christopher Nolan is a British-American director known for intricate plots and non-linear storytelling.
His second feature, a thriller about memory loss, brought him wide critical attention in 2000.
Later he directed a trilogy of superhero films about Gotham's vigilante, then space and dream-heist epics.
Memento is a 2000 psychological thriller written and directed by Christopher Nolan.
The main character is Leonard Shelby, a man who cannot form new memories and hunts for his wife's killer.
Scenes alternate between colour sequences told in reverse and black-and-white sequences told forward.
Leonard relies on tattoos, notes and instant photographs to keep track of what he has learned.
Gladiator is a 2000 historical epic directed by Ridley Scott, not by Christopher Nolan.
The hero is Maximus, a Roman general who is betrayed and enslaved, then fights in the arena.
The story follows his quest for vengeance against the emperor Commodus.
